description:
As an individual participant, I worked on developing the project, exploring its concept, designing the website, and implementing its interactive features. AI-assisted tools were used to support coding, debugging, and content development.

Through this project, I aim to combine technology, creativity, and space exploration to inspire curiosity and preserve the legacy of humanity's missions to the Moon and Mars.
summary:
Lunar & Martian Time Capsule is an interactive website developed to explore and preserve the stories of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. It features an artifact explorer with search and filters, interactive maps showing artifact locations, mission timelines, lifespan comparisons, and a silence counter. Users can also explore artifact details, NASA images, and source links to learn more about each mission.

The project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by bringing attention to abandoned space equipment and presenting its history in an engaging and accessible way. Instead of allowing these artifacts to remain forgotten, it transforms their stories into an interactive digital experience. This project is important because these objects represent humanity's achievements in space exploration, the scientific knowledge gained from past missions, and the legacy of exploration beyond Earth. Our goal is to help people discover, understand, and remember these remarkable artifacts.
details:
Project Details: Lunar & Martian Time Capsule

What does the project do and how does it work?

Lunar & Martian Time Capsule is an interactive website that explores human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions. It allows users to discover these artifacts, learn about their missions, understand their historical importance, and explore where they are located.

The website includes an artifact explorer with search and filtering options, separate Moon and Mars collections, interactive maps with artifact locations, and a mission timeline. It also features a lifespan comparison chart, a silence counter, individual artifact details, NASA images, and source links. These features help users explore the artifacts in an organized and engaging way.

What benefits does it have?

The project makes information about abandoned space equipment easier to access and understand. It brings together historical information, locations, images, and mission details in one place. It can benefit students, educators, researchers, and space enthusiasts by encouraging curiosity and making space exploration history more interactive.

What is the intended impact?

Our aim is to preserve the stories of forgotten space exploration equipment and increase awareness of the scientific missions behind them. These artifacts are more than objects left on another world; they represent human innovation, scientific discoveries, and important achievements in space exploration. The project encourages people to appreciate the legacy of past missions and understand that even when a mission ends, its contribution remains.

What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed as a web application using:

  • HTML: To structure the website and its content.
  • CSS: To create the layout, visual design, and styling.
  • JavaScript: To implement interactive features such as search, filters, maps, timelines, and artifact details.
  • NASA Image and Video Library API: To access relevant NASA images and visual resources.

The project was developed using software-based tools and does not require specialized hardware.

How is the project creative?

The creative idea behind the project is to present abandoned space equipment as a digital time capsule. Instead of simply listing old equipment, the website allows users to explore its location, mission history, operational lifespan, and time since its last communication where that information is available. Combining maps, timelines, images, and interactive artifact details turns historical information into an engaging exploration experience.

What factors were considered?

The main factors considered during development were ease of use, accessibility of information, historical relevance, visual presentation, and educational value. The website was designed to make exploration simple for users with different levels of knowledge about space. We also considered the importance of presenting artifact information alongside sources so that users can learn more about the missions and verify the information.
